sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Setup and purpose
sections.what: Imports the browser library and file tools, and explains that the script runs in GitHub Actions.
sections.why: The comment states the reason: IEEE pages are reachable from that runner.
sections.watch_out: The script depends on the browser library and on IEEE's page layout, so changes on their side can break it.

sections.name: papers
sections.title: List of paper pages to capture
sections.what: Maps four short IDs to IEEE Xplore addresses, then starts a browser and sets a desktop screen size and user agent.
sections.why: Keeps the list of papers in one place.
sections.watch_out: Each ID becomes part of a file name, so renaming one changes its screenshot path.

sections.name: results
sections.title: Visits each paper and saves a screenshot
sections.what: For each paper, opens the page, tries to close cookie prompts, rejects blocked or error pages, saves a screenshot, and records success or the error. It then writes manifest.json and prints the results.
sections.why: Likely reason: the manifest shows which screenshots are real, so the site can use only those.
sections.watch_out: A failed paper is recorded but does not stop the run, so an old screenshot can stay in place while the manifest says it failed.

summary: Saves screenshots of four published IEEE Xplore paper pages into the site's images folder and records which captures succeeded.
purpose: Keeps local copies of the portfolio's paper pages.
why: The header says it runs in GitHub Actions because IEEE pages are reachable there.
how: Starts a headless browser, visits each paper, tries to dismiss cookie prompts, rejects blocked or error pages, saves a JPEG screenshot, and writes a manifest of results.
inputs: The hardcoded list of paper addresses and the output folder public/media/snapshots.
outputs: JPEG screenshots, a manifest.json file, and a summary printed to the console.
risks: Depends on IEEE page layout and access. A blocked page is recorded as a failure, but old screenshots are not deleted. The fixed waiting times may be too short on a slow connection.
debug: Read the error text in manifest.json for each paper. Run the same workflow in GitHub Actions, and confirm Playwright's browser is installed.
